question: Do differing circuit sizes or bounds need extra phase 1 runs when one compatible phase 1 with enough capacity covers every circuit?
answer: No. Phase 1 is counted per compatible parameter set used, not per circuit size. A changed size or bound makes a new compiled circuit, which adds only a phase 2. Compatibility sets the count. Soundness requires verified transcripts, each with at least one honest participant.
approvedCardanoCount: In the common two-phase architecture, the exact count is one phase 2 per distinct compiled circuit, including any wrappers, in a frozen circuit inventory, plus one phase 1 per compatible parameter set the inventory uses. Circuits on one curve and format share a phase 1 whose capacity covers the largest of them. An existing compatible phase 1 can be reused. The 235 pre-dedup review identifiers, 20 families and seven layers describe review scope, not a setup count. The inventory is not frozen, so no total can be assigned yet.
approvedCounterConditions: The count holds only if every circuit uses the same curve and format and fits the shared phase-1 capacity. Smaller circuits need no extra phase 1. Each stage yields sound keys only if its transcript verifies and at least one participant in it was honest.
